item.title: Version 3.11.0
item.description:
neoloopy 3.11.0 (build 65)

Companion apps can now ask neoloopy who is signed in and prove it. Everything in the [3.10.0 notes](3.10.0.md) still applies, including the one-time neoloopy index build after upgrading from 3.9.1.

Scope

  • macOS. The macOS app (DMG and Sparkle update) with the embedded neoloopy CLI and MCP server. The app change also lands on iOS with the next iOS submission; Windows, Linux and Android builds are not part of this release.

For companion apps

  • neoloopy whoami. A read-only command, also an MCP tool, that reports the signed-in neoloopy account: signed_in, account_id, email, display_name, issued_at, expires_at and a 30-day identity assertion signed by the neoloopy service (ES256 compact JWS). Signed out, or with no usable assertion, it answers signed_in: false with a reason of missing, expired or invalid, exit code 0 either way. whoami --public-key prints the JWK set to verify the assertion with, so an app beside neoloopy can record which account acted and check it offline without a sign-in of its own. account_id is the identity; email is present only once Supabase has confirmed the address, else null; display_name is the account's own profile text, a label and never an identifier. The MCP tool leaves the assertion out unless asked (include-assertion), so a token does not land in an agent's transcript by default.
  • The app keeps the assertion fresh. While signed in on the desktop app, the assertion is fetched at sign-in and on launch and stored, readable only by you, beside the quant entitlement token; it is removed at sign-out.
  • Dev key for CI and fixtures. A checked-in dev key pair, two fixture tokens and dart run tool/identity_dev_sign.dart mint test identities; LOOPY_IDENTITY_TOKEN and LOOPY_IDENTITY_KEYS point whoami at fixture files. Docs: "Identity for companion apps" in docs/mcp.md.
  • connect-claude --env NAME=VALUE. Writes an env block on the MCP entry it creates, so --vault <dir> --env LOOPY_PETRI=1 --env LOOPY_INGEST=1 serves an ingested vault to an agent without hand-editing the config.
